A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AL4PDE work. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices E–F to v2 Appendices F–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural PDE experiments, including accuracy comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements and generated-data analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, 1D and 3D Navier–Stokes experiments, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: The pool-based learning cycle, ensemble uncertainty and spatially averaged features remain unchanged. Limited procedural extensions include applying BAIT to an aggregated-feature Bayesian regression proxy and testing an SBAL variant that replaces ensemble uncertainty with PINO loss (Sections 4.3 and 5).

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Burgers, KS, CE and periodic 2D CNS. v2 retains these and adds 1D CNS with outgoing boundary conditions and 3D CNS, substantially extending dimensional and boundary-condition coverage (Section 4.4, Table 1 and Appendix B).

E2.justification: BAIT and Latin Hypercube Sampling join Random, SBAL, LCMD, Core-Set and Top-K in the main comparisons, including the retained tasks (Tables 4–9). Figure 8b also adds PINO-loss SBAL and random-sampling comparisons to the existing ensemble-size experiment.

E3.justification: Added protocols include four-step training for 1D CNS and 3D FNO experiments with a 30,000-candidate pool, 64 initial trajectories, 512 trajectories in each validation/test set, batch size 10 and four rounds. Appendix E tests an 8,192-input pool through exhaustion. Table 2 also revises reported 1D/2D FNO parameter counts from 353,154/3,286,310 to 680,834/6,563,110; this does not establish architectural changes or reruns.

E4.justification: Two focused ablations are added: PINO loss versus ensemble uncertainty on Burgers (Figure 8b), and small versus large acquisition pools on CE (Appendix E, Figure 10). Existing architecture, ensemble-size and feature ablations remain, while correlation and selected-data analyses extend to the added CNS cases and comparators.

E5.justification: v2 specifies three seeds for the added 3D CNS experiments. Ten seeds for Burgers, five for the other cases, 95% confidence intervals, and standard deviations for correlations and marginal distributions retain the existing reporting practice. No increased repetition of retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: The original methods' error-table entries are unchanged after matching corresponding tasks. v2 adds substantial BAIT/LHS and 1D/3D CNS results; for example, final KS RMSE is 0.205 for BAIT and 0.222 for LHS, alongside retained Random at 0.229. New ablation and correlation findings are reported. Existing runtime values also change, including Top-K on KS from 29.8 to 20.4 hours in Table 3.

T1.justification: The governing equations, RMSE and ensemble-uncertainty definitions, feature-sketching formula and SineNet mathematical description are retained. No new proofs, theorems or derivations appear; the added DoE and BAIT discussion is descriptive background.

C1.justification: The abstract's reduction of up to 71% and the conclusion's fourfold data-efficiency claim remain. The contribution paragraph expands the best-performing group from SBAL and LCMD to include BAIT, and the conclusion broadens the benchmark description to 1D, 2D and 3D PDEs.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the PINO-loss experiment as showing that this loss provides an ineffective uncertainty proxy, and the pool-size experiment as showing that sufficient candidate diversity is necessary to target difficult dynamics. It also explains resource constraints on 3D evaluation. Existing training-stability, hyperparameter and geometry limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a statement that code and complete experiment configurations are available. It newly specifies 500 training epochs, the default 2,048-trajectory test set and evaluation using only the first ensemble member. Appendices B–C document added CNS settings, 3D model configuration and H100 hardware. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.1 add focused positioning relative to static and sequential design of experiments, including LHS and Bayesian design. Neural Galerkin, theoretical PDE active-learning and PINO references are added, while Hagnberger et al. is removed. The central first-framework positioning remains; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain. Changes include local language corrections, clearer feature terminology, correction of the MAE figure reference, a reproducibility statement and a new Additional Experiments appendix. Existing results and dataset appendices are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 expand from four to six panels, legends and tables gain comparators, and new pool-size, 1D CNS and 3D trajectory displays are added. Marginal-distribution plots are redrawn and reorganized. Replotted trajectory Figures 11–13 introduce time-axis endpoints of 4, 2 and 40 for Burgers, KS and CE, conflicting with Table 1's retained 2, 40 and 4; v1's corresponding axes agreed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's recommendations through BAIT and LHS controls, nonperiodic and 3D evaluations, and targeted tests of acquisition choices and pool exhaustion. Newly explicit settings and the stated availability of code and configurations improve reproducibility. The new trajectory-axis inconsistencies are a localized reporting regression, but the retained numerical evidence and broader comparative evaluation support a substantial net improvement.
